sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said Board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.

the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­

date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Railway Express Agency, 
Inc., or by its employees, in the condi­
tions out of which the said dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale: EO 10622 (signed 1955-07-01, 20 FR 4762, FR issue of 1955-07-06; held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10622.txt read in full) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between the Railway Express Agency and employees represented by the Teamsters, orders a report within thirty days, and restates the statutory standstill. The FR page prints a Civil Service Commission Part 6 amendment in the neighbouring column (offsets 1552-2618); the dossier's machine clauses mixed it in, so the inventory is corrected by three inventory_overrides covering the whole operative text (offsets 2884-3247, 3248-3384, 3385-3705); the recitals are not operative. Rulings applied: report deadline (2026-10-21; a board order ends on express revocation, and the report date and standstill end are recorded as spent later events with a 'functionally spent' note), unnamed instruments (end is the instrument naming the order). The board report is held (PEB-111-Report.pdf, nmb.gov, jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10622_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10622_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_e26d59e5ee.txt): transmittal dated August 1, 1955 (offsets 1235-1251); the standstill therefore ran through August 31, 1955 (inclusive reading; alternative August 30). First and whole-order end: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237; held text offsets 691-966; '10622' at offset 10521; no effective-date wording, so effective on signing). D6: the dossier chain, actor provisions and missing list name only EO 12553; the draft's later-event proposals name only EO 12553 (OFR catalog and 1989 Codification); the by-number scan finds no other acting instrument. No conflicts were listed. Functionally spent on 1955-08-31; on the books until 1986-02-25. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, 51 FR 7237, read for heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966, the number and subject table and the editorial note and signature block from offset 32923): no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording. Own-residual check, reading EO 10622 in full (offsets 1011-3832 of the order's text, skipping the CSC column at 1552-2618): it created a temporary fact-finding board and restated the statutory standstill; it created no fund, property or private right, and the standstill rested on RLA sec. 10 and ran out in 1955. Nothing of the order outlives its revocation. Bounded search: both texts read; by-number scan of the 6,652 held FR order texts; the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR), which report no current-law hit.
